hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $7y + 3y$ by itself first. Both terms count $y$, so they make $10y$. Then deal with the plain numbers the same way.
There are two kinds of terms here. Keep each minus sign with the number right after it.
Group the $y$ terms as $7y + 3y$ and the numbers as $-2 + 5$. Work out each group.
$7y + 3y = 10y$ and $-2 + 5 = 3$, so the simplified expression is $10y + 3$.

explanation: Sort the terms into $y$ terms ($7y$ and $3y$) and constants ($-2$ and $5$).
Combine the $y$ terms by adding coefficients: $7y + 3y = 10y$.
Combine the constants, keeping the sign of each: $-2 + 5 = 3$.
The simplified expression is $10y + 3$, with one $y$ term and one number.
